co_ridge_1_aka_stairway_to_heaven.blurb: Ridge One is the first big rib of rock on the north side of Skunk Canyon, in the quiet western Flatirons above Boulder. The rock is better than average for the Flatirons, and the ridge mixes long, easy scrambling-style trad with a handful of steep bolted lines. Stairway to Heaven (5.4, trad) and Love (5.4, trad) are the gentle classics, while the overhanging wall low on the ridge holds hard sport lines such as The Guardian (5.12d, sport), Heaven and Hell (5.13a, sport) and Later Creators (5.13b, sport). Expect few other parties, a hike of well under an hour and plenty of poison ivy in season.

co_pages_wall_area_the.blurb: The Pages Wall is one section of The Book, the most popular formation on Lumpy Ridge above Estes Park. The granite here is technical and demands careful footwork, and nearly all the climbing is traditional crack and corner work over one to three pitches. Most lines fall between 5.10 and 5.11, with a few easier and harder outliers. Cheap Date (5.10b, trad), Fat City Crack (5.10c, trad, 3p) and Outlander (5.10d, trad, 2p) are the standouts, with views across to Longs Peak from the upper pitches. Weekends bring crowds, so weekdays are calmer.
co_pages_wall_area_the.parking_note: Use the lot at the end of Lumpy Ridge Road north of Estes Park, or the newer paved trailhead off MacGregor Avenue.
co_pages_wall_area_the.approach: From the trailhead, hike west past the Twin Owls formation and follow the Black Canyon Trail to The Book, adding roughly another two-thirds of a mile beyond Twin Owls. Scramble up to the base of the Pages Wall.

co_burro_wall.blurb: Burro Wall is the lower end of a long limestone cliff band high above Main Elk Creek, outside New Castle. Every line here is bolted, and the bulk fall in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with a few 5.10s and a couple of 5.13s. Appetite For Construction (5.11c, sport), Burro Quality (5.11c, sport) and Sand People Cometh (5.12a, sport) are good ones to start with. The base of each route can be loose and dirty, but the upper sections are cleaner, so a helmet is wise and a stick-clip helps with the first bolts. The south-facing wall soaks up sun, which makes it a popular choice in cooler months.
co_burro_wall.parking_note: Drive Main Elk Road (County Road 243) about six miles from New Castle and park in the big pullout just past the bridge over Main Elk Creek.
co_burro_wall.approach: From the pullout, follow the gravel road for around half a mile until a small cairn on the left marks a faint path through the scrub oak. Follow it up toward the cliff band; the routes begin some distance above its lowest point.

co_cadillac_crag.blurb: Cadillac Crag is a cluster of four rock fins northwest of Rincon in Eldorado Canyon State Park, on the conglomerate sandstone that gives Eldo its character. It is mostly trad, with a few bolted faces, and the grades run from easy fifth class up into the low 5.12s, with the bulk between 5.10 and 5.11. Arete, dihedral and finger-to-hand crack climbing are all on offer. Gonzo (5.8, trad), V3 (5.8, trad) and Deviant (5.10a, trad) suit moderate leaders, and Brand New Cadillac (5.11b/c, sport) is a bolted option. The hike is longer than at most Eldo crags but pays off with big views.
co_cadillac_crag.approach: Walk a short stretch up the road from the small lot at the canyon's end to the Eldo Trail, then take the Rincon Cutoff Trail. Where it crosses talus, keep going up the ridge toward the fins and finish with a scramble up talus to the base.

co_thumb_the.blurb: The Thumb is a short granite spire on Prospect Mountain, just above Estes Park, with views over town to the peaks. Climbs are one or two pitches and the style is a blend of bolted sport lines and a larger number of trad routes, plus a few top-rope faces. Grades span from very easy up to 5.12 and beyond, with a lot of 5.10 and 5.11 in the middle. Vapor Trail (5.12d, sport), Confines of Power (5.12a, sport) and Green Thumb (5.7, sport, 2p) are the highlights. The crag sits beside the Needle, so a day can link both. Faces pointing north, east and west can stay damp and lichenous.
co_thumb_the.approach: A signed trail leaves the Peak View Drive lot and climbs about three-quarters of a mile, gaining roughly 400 feet, to reach the Needle and then the Thumb a little farther uphill.

co_pandemic_caves.blurb: Pandemic Caves is a set of three small boulder caves at different heights along the trail through Mitchell Creek Canyon, south of Denver near Castle Rock. The climbing is mainly steep and overhung, on pocketed rock with rough, grainy topouts. Problems range from V0 to V11, with a good number of easier lines in the V0 to V2 range and a harder tier above V6. Murder Hornet (V5, bouldering) and Murder Hornet Stand (V4, bouldering) are the best known. Landings are near the trail so bring pads and be ready to share space with hikers. Rattlesnakes are seen around the formations in warm weather.
co_pandemic_caves.parking_note: Use the Gateway Mesa Open Space parking area, which reaches all the canyon's bouldering.
co_pandemic_caves.approach: Follow the canyon trail past Corona Crag. The first cave is right beside the path on the left, with the others a little farther up on the same side.

co_white_cliff.blurb: White Cliff is a small slab crag on the north side of I-70 in 10 Mile Canyon near Frisco, at roughly 9,500 feet. The rock is a mix of polished, exfoliating stone, so test holds and watch for loose blocks. Nearly everything is bolted face, slab and roof climbing, in the 5.6 to 5.11 range with most routes between 5.7 and 5.9. Love Handles (5.6, sport), Bubba (5.7, sport) and Funky Gunky (5.9, sport) are good picks. The wall faces southeast and gets sun until mid-afternoon, and the short hike makes it easy to squeeze in after work. Ticks can be thick in spring.
co_white_cliff.parking_note: Take Frisco exit 201 and drive west on I-70 for a bit under a mile, then pull off beside the aspens near the forest service sign.
co_white_cliff.approach: Follow the steep path through the trees from the pullout. Bear left for the West Wall, or right to reach the East and Far East Walls.

co_ridge_1.blurb: Ridge 1 is the first of the numbered crags on Eldorado Mountain, south of Eldorado Canyon near Boulder. It has a remote, wilderness feel because of the long walk, and few other parties show up. Almost everything is bolted, and the climbing is harder than at neighboring ridges: the heart of it is 5.11 and 5.12, with a handful of 5.13s and one 5.14. The farthest section has the best continuous rock with big overhangs. The Fornicator (5.11c, sport), The Adultress (5.12b, sport) and Arrogant Bastard (5.12c, sport) are among the most-recommended lines. Poison ivy grows around the area.
co_ridge_1.approach: Follow the main trail west, past the branch that goes to Ridge 2, and stay on it until it delivers you to the south tip of the crag. The route around the hill is long.

co_diamond_the.blurb: The Diamond is the huge granite east face of Longs Peak in Rocky Mountain National Park, a 900-foot alpine wall above 13,000 feet. Routes are long, sustained crack and face pitches, with most of the free climbs between 5.10 and 5.12 and a few aid lines. Casual Route (5.10b, alpine) is the most popular and Pervertical Sanctuary (5.11a, alpine), D7 (5.11c, alpine) and Ariana (5.12a, alpine, 6p) are standouts. Reaching the base takes a long day with a big hike and a loose, serious scramble up the North Chimney, so most parties start in the dark. The free-climbing window is a short one in midsummer, and the wall can be crowded.
co_diamond_the.approach: From the Longs Peak trailhead hike to Chasm Lake, then work around its north shore to the base of the East Face. The usual way up is the North Chimney, a loose fourth to low fifth class gully that leads to Broadway Ledge.

co_seal_rock.blurb: Seal Rock stands out among the Flatirons above Boulder, on the south side of Bear Canyon. Its radically overhanging south face carries some of the hardest sport routes in the area, on steep sandstone with pockets and tufa-like flutings. The bulk of what is here sits at 5.12 and 5.13, with a few 5.14s, including Thunder Muscle (5.14a, sport), I Am The Walrus (5.14a/b, sport) and Choose Life (5.13c, sport). Super Tuscan (5.13b, sport) and The Stoop (5.12b, sport) are other standouts. The north and east sides hold slab and multipitch lines, such as East Face North Side/Seal Rock (5.4, trad). Expect a steep, demanding hike in.
co_seal_rock.approach: From the Mesa Trail, take the unsigned Harmon Cave Trail up and west, passing the gated cave, then climb steeply south to the base. Stay left for the south face or right for the north face.
